# Silo

> Silo is Sharpnr's all-in-one data platform. It provides S3-compatible object storage with CDN-backed delivery, a Drive with folders, previews and sharing for everyday files, managed PostgreSQL with a controlled database explorer, and a data lake and warehouse for analytics — all on one platform, behind one API, under one permission model, with one audit trail.

Status: early access, onboarding the first organizations. Object storage, Drive and CDN delivery are furthest along; PostgreSQL provisioning and the data lake follow; the warehouse and cross-region backups come after that. Nothing on this site should be read as generally available today.

The defining boundary: **Sharpnr Engine owns business logic. Silo owns storage and data resources.** Silo is deliberately not the Hospitality, Accounting, HR, or CRM database — it is the layer those applications provision resources from.

Key facts:

- Vendor: Sharpnr (https://sharpnr.com)
- Product site: https://silo.sharpnr.com
- Services: object storage, Drive, CDN, managed PostgreSQL, data lake, data warehouse, backups
- Object API: S3-compatible, so existing SDKs and CLI tools work unchanged
- Databases provisioned: PostgreSQL only. Organizations never receive superuser credentials.
- Database explorer: controlled operations only. No arbitrary SQL editor yet; a full SQL workspace comes after the controlled explorer matures.
- Drive: folders, in-browser previews, sharing by link or by person with expiry, version history, desktop sync, per-person quotas.
- Primary data lake format: Parquet. Also supported: JSON, JSONL, CSV, Avro, ORC.
- Permissions: role-based and resource-scoped (Read / Write / Admin), governed centrally in Cortex and enforced by Silo.
- Audit: one append-oriented log covering storage, Drive, databases and datasets together.

- [OpenAPI specification](https://silo.sharpnr.com/v1/openapi.json): Machine-readable API contract between Silo and consuming services.
- [Swagger UI](https://silo.sharpnr.com/swagger-ui): Interactive API explorer.
- [ReDoc](https://silo.sharpnr.com/redoc): API reference documentation.

## Platform

- [Object storage](https://silo.sharpnr.com/#storage): S3-compatible buckets for files, media, attachments, backups, exports and arbitrary objects. Versioning, lifecycle rules, checksums, encryption at rest, and organization- and per-person quotas enforced by Silo rather than by callers. Public objects are addressed independently of the physical storage path, so files move between backends without breaking a shared URL.
- [Drive](https://silo.sharpnr.com/#drive): The human-facing view over the same storage — a folder tree with drag-and-drop upload, in-browser previews for documents, images and video, sharing by link or by person with expiry, version history and restore, desktop sync, and full-text search scoped to what the viewer may see.
- [PostgreSQL as a service](https://silo.sharpnr.com/#postgres): Silo creates the database, creates organization-scoped roles (org_123_app, org_123_migrator, org_123_readonly, org_123_admin), applies permissions, generates credentials, and returns a connection string. Connection pooling, read replicas and point-in-time recovery are included. The physical cluster is an implementation detail and superuser is never issued.
- [Database explorer](https://silo.sharpnr.com/#postgres): Browse schemas, tables, views, functions, indexes, constraints and rows through controlled operations, with scoped read queries and result limits. The browser talks HTTPS to Silo; Silo talks to PostgreSQL. The browser never connects to PostgreSQL directly.
- [Data lakes and warehouses](https://silo.sharpnr.com/#data): Raw, refined and curated zones with partitioned Parquet datasets, ingestion from PostgreSQL, files, events and scheduled jobs, then ETL/ELT into analytical warehouses with a query engine and analytics APIs.
- [CDN delivery](https://silo.sharpnr.com/#storage): Edge caching for public objects, custom domains with managed certificates, signed URLs for time-limited private delivery, and invalidation by path or prefix.
- [All services](https://silo.sharpnr.com/#services): Object storage, Drive, CDN, PostgreSQL, data lake, warehouse and backups, with what is available today versus in early access.

## Evaluating Silo

- [Comparison](https://silo.sharpnr.com/#compare): How Silo compares to hyperscaler storage plus managed Postgres, backend platforms, and self-assembled stacks — including the cases where Silo is the wrong choice.
- [FAQ](https://silo.sharpnr.com/#faq): Availability, what can be stored, how Drive differs from object storage, supported databases, superuser policy, the no-raw-SQL decision, S3 compatibility, the shared permission model and audit trail, large-file handling, and lake formats.

## Optional

- [Sharpnr](https://sharpnr.com): The parent company. Sharpnr Engine is the business-logic platform that consumes Silo resources.
